new_statements.quote: Moji and Laghuu, in contrast with the rest of the Muji clade, both yield /55/ as the dominant synchronic reflex of TC-2, but the two languages do not pattern very closely in their distribution of /55/
new_statements.citation: Pelkey, Jamin R. 2011. Dialectology as Dialectic: Interpreting Phula Variation. Trends in Linguistics Studies and Monographs 229. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton. Ch. 6 'The language clades of Phula Proper', sec. 6.3.1 'Tone system innovations', Table 6.3 'Unmarked tonal reflex patterns in Phula and other [Ngwi languages]' (pp. 275-276) and Tables 6.4-6.7 'Muji clade tone correspondences for TC-1 / TC-2 / TC-3 / *checked classes TC-L and TC-H' (pp. 288-293). doi:10.1515/9783110245851.271
new_statements.locator: ch. 6, sec. 6.3.1 'Tone system innovations' and Table 6.3 (pp. 275-276), per Google Books snippets of volume fGoZL4h4qFMC; table row snippet: 'Moji 52/55/33 33/55/21 55 52/55 35' / 'Moji 52 33 55 52 35'
new_statements.relation_note: Google Books snippets only (full text paywalled): Table 6.3 lists, per Proto-Ngwi tone class (TC-1, TC-2, TC-3 and the two *checked classes), Moji's synchronic tonal reflexes as '52/55/33 | 33/55/21 | 55 | 52/55 | 35', dominant pattern 'Moji 52 33 55 52 35' (vs. core Muji 33 21 21 33 21); prose: 'Moji and Laghuu, in contrast with the rest of the Muji clade, both yield /55/ as the dominant synchronic reflex of TC-2, but the two languages do not pattern very closely in their distribution of /55/'; 'on the surface Moji tone correspondences in TC-1 appear to match up with little other than the Laghuu preservation of /55/ on *-m.. syllables'; another snippet names 'Moji /52/ and /35/' among mino…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Tonal (Southeastern Ngwi contour-tone system); Moji-LCC reflexes of the five Proto-Ngwi tone classes are predominantly 52, 33, 55, 52, 35, with 55/33/21 as secondary reflexes; nothing on stress.
new_statements.exceptions: Snippet: TC-1 splits conditioned by *nasal-final rhymes in Muji varieties; 'pitch values of TC-2 nasal-initial syllables.. widely irregular'.
new_statements.identity_note: 'Moji' in Pelkey 2011 = his Moji-LCC datapoint (Luchaichong, W Xichou) = ISO [ymi] which he himself requested; the Table 6.3 row is labelled 'Moji' alongside the other Muji-clade languages (Muji-N/S, Bokha, Phuma, Muzi, Qila Muji, Laghuu, Thopho). Already in our bibliography as 'likely states stress; not yet obtained' with the open question 'check whether Moji-LCC tones are tabulated' -- the snippets answer yes.

sources.citation: Pelkey, Jamin R. 2011. A Phula Comparative Lexicon: Phola, Phuza, Muji, Phowa, Azha. SIL Language and Culture Documentation and Description 18. Dallas: SIL International. 144 pp.
sources.note: Only sketch is sec. 3.3 'Southern Muji phonology in brief' (pp. 8-9, datapoint PJZ = Southern Muji [ymc], not Moji): syllable {(C)(V)VT}; 'Regarding suprasegmental phonology, Southern Muji features five pitch contrasts: high-level /55/, mid-level /33/, low-rising /13/, low-falling /21/ and, high-falling /52/' + sandhi + non-contrastive tense voice. Moji [ymi] named only on the clade map (p. 3) and p. 16 ('After an early split of the Moji language [ymi]..'). Zero occurrences of 'stress'/'accent' in the whole book. SILENT; no Moji sketch.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority / Pelkey, Jamin R. 2007. Change Request 2007-120 (split [ymj]; create [ymc], [ymx], [ymq], [ymi] Moji, [ymz]; adopted 2008-01-14) and Request for New Language Code Element [ymi] Moji. SIL International.
sources.note: Nothing on phonology: names, location (Luchaichong, W Xichou Co; S/SW Wenshan Co.), 2,000 speakers, closest = possibly Phuma; Moji 'separated from Muji proper for centuries', core-vocabulary similarity < 60% with other Muji varieties; only source cited is Pelkey (forthcoming 2008) PhD.

sources.note: Group-level only, p. 57-58 (sec. 6 'Phula linguistic features'): 'Most known Phula languages have a tense-lax phonation contrast, and some retain consonant finals.
